coverage: nprobe is out of 4 shards, so a query sees 25% or 50% of the corpus. The recall ceiling is that fraction of a single shard's recall, not 1.0: these rows measure the build and the shard-merge cost, not full-corpus recall. Probing all four shards needs all four resident, about 145 GiB of graph plus vectors, which is what sharding exists to avoid.
provenance: shard 0 overlapped concurrent 100k benchmark runs (a build-knob grid and two FAISS parity runs), which roughly doubled its build time. The three later shards ran alone: 2534-2644 s each, so an uncontended 100M build is about 2.9 h, not 3.65 h. Recall is deterministic at a fixed graph and is unaffected by that load. load1 was not captured: the sharded _meta gained host/cores/load1 after this build started.
gt: exact top-10 over the full corpus, cached; not cross-checked by an independent scan above 1M
